Read-only health check over an organizational demarkus knowledge system. Knowledge-system counterpart to `/soul-doctor` (local soul). **Never writes**: surfaces findings and suggests fixes; the user decides.

Same substrate as the soul: the broker exposes the same `mark_*` tools remotely (`mark_worlds`, `mark_graph`, `mark_backlinks`, `mark_list`, `mark_lookup`, `mark_fetch`, `mark_versions`). Three differences from `/soul-doctor` shape every step:

1. **Multi-world.** URLs are `mark://<world>/<path>`, not bare paths. Enumerate with `mark_worlds`, audit per world.
2. **Broker graph store is ephemeral** (per-pod; resets on restart). `mark_backlinks` returns only what *this* session crawled, so `mark_graph` **must** run before any backlink/orphan reasoning, every run.
3. **Cross-world references are existence-checkable** here (not in a single-world soul audit): `mark_worlds` + complete per-world inventories resolve `mark://<other-world>/<path>`. This un-defers the bare-`mark://` reference check (see Deep checks).

## Scope

From `$ARGUMENTS`:

- **blank** → every joined system, all worlds. Read the validated registry:

  ```bash
  "$HOME/.demarkus/bin/demarkus-plugin" registry knowledge-list
  ```

  One line per system MCP server slug; reach it through the destination server's `mark_*` tools. Successful empty result: nothing joined (suggest `/knowledge-join <broker-url>`), stop. Non-zero exit or malformed output: registry failure, surface and stop.
- **a slug** (e.g. `acme`) → that system, all its worlds.
- **a `mark://<world>/` URL** → resolve to exactly one joined system before auditing.

Explicit world scope: call `mark_worlds` through every joined system's own MCP server, collect `(system slug, world)` matches. Every directory call must succeed before deciding uniqueness or absence; on any failure, surface it and stop with scope resolution incomplete. Audit only after exactly one match is selected. Multiple systems expose the same world name: ask which. No complete directory contains it: report unavailable scope, stop.

Blank or slug scope: `mark_worlds` per resolved system to enumerate readable worlds (note `writable`; a fix suggestion is actionable only on a world the user can publish to), audit each. Enumeration fails or malformed: surface the error, mark that system incomplete, suppress full-coverage conclusions for it, continue only with unrelated systems whose enumeration succeeded. Explicit world scope: audit only the selected `(system slug, world)` pair; never expand back to every readable world. Anchor each audited world on `mark://<world>/index.md`. Key all graph, inventory, and report state by both system slug and world name; never merge same-named worlds from different systems.

> **Read-auth caveat.** `mark_lookup` is filtered to what your token may read; `mark_worlds` lists only readable worlds. The audit covers *your* visibility, not the whole system. Say so; never imply full coverage of a world or system you can't fully see.

Before the first broker call, set a command-wide deadline five minutes out. Check it before every MCP call. On expiry: stop starting calls, preserve completed results, list skipped work, mark affected worlds incomplete, suppress conclusions needing missing coverage. The deadline cannot cancel an in-flight call; disclose when relevant.

## Gather (per world)

1. **Crawl the link graph.** `mark_graph` on `mark://<world>/index.md` with `depth: 5`. Also **populates the ephemeral graph store** for this session, required before `mark_backlinks` returns anything. Parse:
   - **Nodes:** `[status] <url> "title" N links`: note any status not `ok`, and `(no title)`.
   - **Edges:** `<from> -> <to>`: `mark://` targets internal (possibly cross-world); `http(s)` external.
2. **Inventory.** Directory queue starting with `mark_list mark://<world>/` and `include_archived: true`. Follow each `next-cursor` as `cursor` until `complete: true`, preserving `include_archived: true`; enqueue every returned subdirectory, repeat until the queue is empty. One root page is neither recursive nor necessarily complete. Track visited directory URLs and a per-directory seen-cursor set; every incomplete page must return a non-empty cursor, different from the request cursor, unseen for that directory. Bound: 1,000 total list calls (initial and continuation) or 20,000 documents per world. A bound makes coverage incomplete only when another required call or document remains; a terminal complete page at the exact bound with an empty queue is exhaustive.

   Any failure, truncating limit, partial-result marker, or unavailable subtree makes the inventory incomplete. Preserve returned entries, list missing scope and exact coverage, suppress definitive orphan, missing-hub, broken-link, and dangling-reference conclusions that depend on omitted paths. Cross-world conclusions use only complete inventories and crawls from worlds in the same resolved system and audit scope.
3. **Crawl disconnected documents.** For every inventory document absent from the root crawl's successful nodes, including `[error]` nodes, `mark_graph` on that document with depth 1. Captures outbound edges from orphaned, failed, and beyond-depth documents.
4. **Bound supplemental crawling.** At most 100 supplemental `mark_graph` calls per command, retries included, within the deadline. Report skipped documents and mark affected worlds incomplete when either limit hits.
5. **Retry once.** Retry each unsuccessful source once while budget remains. A final source failure leaves only that source's outbound edges unknown: mark that world's orphan analysis incomplete, cross-world orphan analysis incomplete for every in-scope world that source could link into (a target world's orphan verdict needs every in-scope source world fully crawled), and broken-link analysis incomplete for edges that source would contribute; `[not-found]` findings already confirmed by successful sources stand.

## Core checks (graph + inventory; per-doc fetching only for the bounded broken-link confirmations below)

- **Broken links**: an edge whose `mark://` target does not exist. **Crawl-node status says what's already confirmed:**
  - Target **in Nodes as `[not-found]`**: *already confirmed broken*; the broker said not-found. Report directly; **do not re-fetch** (N re-confirmations are N wasted calls).
  - Target **absent from Nodes**: may sit beyond crawl depth; a complete in-scope inventory (`mark_list`) settles it. **Same-world**: check the world's inventory. **Cross-world** `mark://<other>/…`: check that world's complete inventory only when it is in the selected scope. Target world out of scope, unreadable, or either inventory incomplete: classify unresolved, not broken. A complete `mark_list` is still read-filtered (entries the token cannot read are dropped), so absence from it is not proof: confirm a same-world suspect with one `mark_fetch`, report broken only on explicit `not-found`; unauthorized or any other failure leaves it unresolved.
  - Target present as **`[error]`**: not a missing doc; next check.
- **Unroutable / cross-system references**: an `[error]` node on a `mark://` link means the broker couldn't route the host. `mark_worlds` lists only readable worlds, so absence there does **not** prove the host is external. Readable host: retry once, report a persistent dispatch failure. Otherwise unresolved (possibly unreadable, cross-system, or stale); never claim absence or externality without independent evidence.
- **Orphans**: an inventory document never the target of any `mark://` edge after complete root and supplemental crawls, and not the world's root hub. Report successful crawl coverage. Cross-world inbound links count only from fully crawled worlds in the same resolved system and scope; other systems cannot prove or disprove orphan status.
- **Stale index entries**: broken links whose source is a hub/index doc (`index.md`).
- **Missing hub**: a subtree with documents but no `index.md`.
- **Untitled docs**: **`[ok]`** nodes shown `(no title)` (no H1 / declared title). `(no title)` on a `not-found`/`error` node is the broken-link/cross-system finding above, **not** untitled; don't double-report.
- **ADR sequence**: per `adr/` directory, flag duplicate or gapped `NNNN` prefixes only when that directory's inventory is complete. Failed, truncated, skipped, or partial coverage: report inconclusive with exact coverage.

## Deep checks (per-doc `mark_fetch`; bounded scope, or when asked)

One fetch per document: run only for a single world, or when the user asks for a thorough audit. Fetch at most 100 documents. If capped or sampled, report exact coverage and skipped count; never imply full coverage.

- **Untagged docs**: fetch, check `tags` non-empty. Untagged docs are findable only by title or explicit path. (Publish gate prevents new ones; this finds pre-existing.)
- **Metadata lost across versions** *(legacy servers)*: an untagged doc that **used to** carry tags. Brokers before the APPEND metadata merge passed only `{agent: …}` on append, dropping `tags`, `importance`, `title`, `type`, and with them the **policy tag axes** satisfied at publish time: compliant turns noncompliant with no write rejected. Retire once the catalog is clean. Run only on docs the untagged or policy-axis check flagged that have more than one version:
  1. `mark_versions`. `chain-valid` false: report the `chain-error`, mark the doc **inconclusive**; metadata from a broken chain is not evidence.
  2. Fetch versions newest-first below current (`mark_fetch mark://<world>/<path>/v<N>`) until one carries `tags` **and** satisfies the policy's required axes and `require_fields`; a version that was itself noncompliant is not a repair, keep walking, say so if none qualifies. At most 10 fetches per doc and 100 calls total for this check, `mark_versions` included; when the budget is gone, stop, list skipped or truncated docs, treat a hit found after truncating as low-confidence.
  3. Report recovered `tags`/`importance`/`type`/`title` and their source version as a **repair candidate**. Any failed call leaves the doc inconclusive; never infer metadata a call did not return.

  Untagged since `v1`: never tagged, a curation exercise. *Lost* tags: a candidate, not a verdict; a later `mark_publish` may have dropped them deliberately. Appends between the two versions point at legacy damage, a publish at intent. Get user confirmation before restoring.

  Repair, as a separate write step (this command never writes): `mark_fetch` with **`force=true`** (plain fetch returns an outline for bodies of 8KB or more; publishing an outline destroys the doc). Version differs from the audited one: another writer moved it, re-run the check. Then `mark_publish` that body with the current metadata map **plus** the recovered fields (publish replaces the map; an omission deletes opaque keys), re-checked against current policy axes and `require_fields`, `retention` only if the user asks, `expected_version` at current, `on_conflict: "fail"`. On any error or conflict: report exactly, stop, say the doc is unchanged.
- **Policy-axis noncompliance** *(knowledge-only)*: fetch `mark://root/.well-known/demarkus/policy.md` once; read **required tag axes** (e.g. `category:`) and **`require_fields:`** (e.g. `type`). Flag each fetched doc missing any required `axis:value` tag or field. Likely published before the requirement, or via a `warn` gate. Report the missing axis/field and policy strictness (`warn`/`block`/`ask`).
- **Untyped docs (OKF `type`)**: read `type` metadata; flag **missing or `Document`** (generic default) so they can be typed (`Reference`/`Decision`/`Architecture`/`Plan`/`Journal`/`Guide`/…). **Exempt `index.md` and `log.md`**: missing type is correct there. If policy lists `type` under `require_fields:`, only a missing type on a non-exempt doc is **noncompliance**; `type=Document` satisfies presence and stays an advisory backfill candidate unless policy defines an allowed-type constraint excluding it. Without a required field, both are advisory. Fix: re-publish with an explicit `metadata.type`.
- **In-body frontmatter block** *(demarkus-specific)*: body whose **first non-blank line is `---`** with reserved/operational keys (`version`, `previous-hash`, `archived`, `meta.*`): almost always an **exported demarkus doc pasted back into a publish**. Frontmatter is stored out-of-band; a body-leading `---` is literal content: stray horizontal rule, garbled headings, stale `version:` (won't match the real fetched `version`). Flag; fix is strip the block and re-publish with metadata as request metadata.
- **Style-guide violations** (`mark://root/.well-known/demarkus/style.md`): per fetched body flag **em dashes** anywhere (banned; count per doc) and **duplicate headings** within one document (headings are `#section` anchors; a duplicate takes a `-1` suffix that shifts when sections move, silently breaking inbound anchors; exclude `#` lines inside fenced code). Fix: re-publish with unique headings and em dashes replaced by comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses. The style gate (default `warn`, `DEMARKUS_STYLE_STRICTNESS` adjusts) catches these at write time; this finds the pre-existing corpus.
- **Duplicate content**: compare `content-hash` across fetched docs; identical hashes under different paths (even different worlds) are duplicates.
- **Dangling & unlinked references**: a relationship in *prose* (or inline code) the link graph never captured, because only `[text](url)` becomes an edge. "supersedes ADR 0005" is invisible to every graph check above. Per fetched body, scan for high-confidence patterns; resolve each against the **inventory** (existence) and the **doc's own parsed links** (already-linked?); no fetches beyond this tier's bodies:
  - **Patterns** (tight set; prose false positives are worse than a missed edge):
    - ADR references: `ADR[ -]?#?\d{3,4}` (case-insensitive). Canonical target: inventory path matching `<world>/adr/NNNN-*.md`.
    - Bare/inline `mark://<world>/<path>` URLs **not** inside `[text](…)`: a reference that lost its link syntax. **Viable here** (unlike the soul audit): resolve readable hosts against the selected system's `mark_worlds`, then check that world's complete in-scope inventory for the path. Host belongs only to another system, unreadable, out of scope, or inventory incomplete: unresolved, not dangling. Still **exclude** inline-code placeholders (`` `mark://host/...` `` with ellipses) and fenced code.
  - **Exclude**: the doc's *own* ADR number (self-reference), and any mention inside a fenced (```` ``` ````/`~~~`) block; `# ADR 0005` in a code sample is not a reference (same fence-skip rule as the catalog's `firstH1`).
  - **Resolve "already-linked?" against the citing body's OWN markdown links, NOT the crawl's edge store.** The crawl seeds from the hub, so an **orphan** is never visited and its outbound links never enter the (ephemeral) store; keying off edges would falsely flag an orphan's real `[…](…)` link as unlinked. Matters *more* on the broker, where the store is per-session. Every body is already held; parse each for its own `[text](url)` links and check whether one resolves to the mention's target.
  - **Classify** each surviving mention:
    - **Unlinked reference**: target *exists* (same- or cross-world) but the citing body has **no markdown link** to it. Reachable, not traversable. Fix: `[ADR 0005](mark://<world>/adr/0005-…md)`.
    - **Dangling reference**: resolves to **no doc** in any complete in-scope world inventory of the same resolved system. Confirm against those inventories, not `mark_lookup` (misses untagged docs). Fix: restore the doc, or correct/remove the reference. If the citing doc itself annotates the absence ("no md file exists"), report **known**, not actionable.

  Distinct from **Broken links**: that follows an *edge* to a missing target; this finds references that never were edges.

## Report

Plain, grouped by world then check, most actionable first. One-line summary per system first (`<system>: <W> worlds, <N> docs, <X> findings`). Shape:

```text
## <system> hygiene report

### mark://<world>/  (<N> docs, writable: yes/no)   [coverage: your read scope]

#### Broken links (<n>)
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md → mark://<world>/<missing>.md  ([not-found] node, confirmed): fix the link or restore the target

#### Unresolved / unroutable references (<n>)
- mark://<world>/index.md → mark://unknown/index.md  ([error], non-member or unreadable host): unresolved; verify system membership/read access before deciding whether it is stale or external

#### Orphans (<n>)
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: no inbound `mark://` edge after complete in-scope crawling; add an appropriate inbound catalog link

#### In-body frontmatter (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/index.md: body opens with a `---` block whose in-body version differs from the stored version; strip it, re-publish with out-of-band metadata

#### Untyped: OKF type missing/Document (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: type=Document (or none); set a `type` key in metadata, e.g. {"type":"Reference"}  (index.md/log.md exempt)

#### Policy-axis noncompliance (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: missing required axis `category:` (policy strictness: block); re-publish with the axis tag

#### Dangling & unlinked references (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/adr/0006-….md → "ADR 0005", dangling: no such doc in any complete in-scope world inventory; restore or drop the reference
- mark://<world>/architecture.md → "ADR 0006", unlinked: target exists but no in-body link; convert the prose mention to a [link](mark://…)

#### Metadata lost across versions (<n>)        [deep check, scanned <k>/<N> docs]
- mark://<world>/<doc>.md: candidate: tagged at v3 (category:ops + 6 tags, importance 0.7), none at v7; repair = force-fetch v7, publish that body with v7's metadata map plus the v3 fields (policy axes and require_fields re-checked), `expected_version: 7`, `on_conflict: "fail"`

#### Untagged / ADR / index / titles / duplicates …
```

End with a short prioritized "what I'd fix first." Verdict: "all clean" only when every check ran to complete coverage and found nothing. Incomplete coverage (deadline, crawl failure, inventory bound, deep-check cap): report every confirmed finding as usual, then state coverage incomplete with the gaps listed; "no findings in the covered scope" only when there are zero findings.

## Don't

- Don't write to any world or modify any document. Read-only. A requested fix is a separate, explicit step, only against a `writable` world.
- Don't skip the crawl. The graph store is **ephemeral**; `mark_backlinks` is empty until `mark_graph` populates it this session. Empty after crawling is a real signal; empty *before* is an un-primed store.
- Don't fabricate. `mark_worlds` returns nothing readable, a hub is `not-found`, or `~/.demarkus/knowledge-systems` is empty: say so and stop.
- Don't imply coverage you don't have. Read-auth scopes visibility; disclose the bound (which worlds, how many docs, deep-check sample size).
- Don't confuse with `/soul-doctor` (personal, local soul). This audits the shared, broker-fronted system(s).
